speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the character of your stool, such as whether it contains blood, mucus, or undigested food?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the relief of pain by defecation and urgency strongly suggest inflammatory bowel disease or irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea. Given your recent camping trip, could you tell me if anyone else in your party has been diagnosed with an infection or if you experienced fever at the time? Also, have you noticed any unintentional weight loss or blood in your stool?

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Ulcerative Colitis)

The history of bloody/mucoid stool, urgent bowel movements relieved by defecation, and a "feeling of incomplete evacuation" are classic signs of inflammatory bowel disease, specifically Ulcerative Colitis. While the camping trip suggests a potential infectious trigger, the chronic nature and specific symptom pattern point toward an inflammatory condition. I need to confirm this with further testing.

REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Calprotectin
REQUEST IMAGES: Colonoscopy
